chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no Penalty (Hadd) for the one upon whom there is no Penalty (Hadd).

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.حَدّ: Fixed legal penalty or punishment prescribed by Sharia for specific crimes
key_terms.عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi, a prominent narrator in Shia hadith collections

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'La Hadd liman la hadd 'alayh' in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi articulates the principle of 'absence of proof implies absence of obligation,' serving as a foundational rule in Shia usul al-fiqh for determining when fixed punishments (Hudud) are suspended. It underscores the juristic rigor required to ensure that penalties are not applied unless all specific conditions and impediments are fully satisfied, reflecting the Shia emphasis on precision in legal application. This maxim is frequently cited by scholars like Al-Shaykh al-Mufid and Al-Tusi to argue against the arbitrary extension of Hudud beyond their strict textual definitions.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘There is no Penalty (Hadd) for the one upon whom there is no Penalty (Hadd)’.
